rows: Addition
Adds another point that supports or extends the same idea.
Similarity
Shows that the next idea is like the one before it.
Contrast
Shows that the next idea differs from or goes against the one before it.
Concession
Admits a point, then says something that still holds in spite of it.
Cause and effect
Shows that one thing leads to, or explains, another.
Example
Gives a specific case of the general idea before it.
Emphasis
Stresses or strengthens the point just made.
Restatement
Says the same idea again in different, often clearer, words.
Sequence
Shows the order of events or steps in time.
Summary
Sums up the ideas that came before.
Condition
Shows what follows if something is, or isn't, the case.
Generalization
States what is usually or broadly true.
Attitude
Shows how the writer feels about the point that follows, such as good news or a surprise.
Place
Shows where something is compared with what was just described.
Repetition
Points back to something that already happened or was already said.
Replacement
Shows that one thing takes the place of another.
